foundation: Barrot V3 execution, verification, security and preservation
latest_findings: Coinbase Financial Markets originated CFTC Letter 26-05. The request covers customer digital-asset collateral and FCM proprietary payment-stablecoin residual interest.

USDC is issued by Circle Internet Financial, LLC for non-EEA holders. Its public issuer, reserve and attestation disclosures strongly match the pre-GENIUS payment-stablecoin criteria; Circle National Trust and Circle New York Trust are separate regulated affiliates, not current issuers.

CFTC Letter 26-05 allows payment stablecoins in 30.7 accounts without DCO acceptance under FCM valuation/haircut policies; futures and cleared-swaps accounts require DCO acceptance. FCM-owned payment stablecoins may be deposited as residual interest subject to capital charge.
RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody, a NY limited-purpose trust company; its government-MMF reserve holdings need look-through. Ripple National Trust Bank is not the current issuer.
Circle USDC is natively issued on XRPL. BNY is a shared custody node: Circle Reserve Fund USDXX is custodied there, BNY is primary RLUSD reserve custodian, and BNY supports XRP/RLUSD custody.
Standard Chartered RLUSD custody on XRPL is live; LMAX collateral integration is planned. Bitnomial currently lists XRP collateral but not USDC/RLUSD.
key_unknowns: No CFTC-specific determination naming USDC or RLUSD.
No FCM notice of reliance or actual stablecoin/XRP collateral/residual-interest balances.
RLUSD government-MMF look-through and October signed attestation unavailable.
No actual XRP purchase or inventory change caused by stablecoin collateral established.
